deployment_incident.user_latest_instruction: Prepare and validate candidates first, notify the user, and let the user arrange Termux restart. No further automatic APK replacement or server restart.

limits: Native submissions and SF whole-X11 content-layer presentation are separate measurements. No proof of sustained 120 distinct page images per second.
The desktop/process environment restarted between snapshots. These results are directional samples, not a tightly controlled alternating A/B.
Diagnostic trace affects timing and is not a normal-FPS sample. Tick markers precede gate reopening, so not every crossing marker requires a ready permit at that instant.
No whole-device power, precise input latency, or long-term stability result.
remaining_work: Locate remaining Surface delivery misses with low-overhead per-frame correlation.
Optimize demonstrable GPU/CPU work while preserving clipping, ownership and lifecycle correctness.
Verify actual page-content presentation near 120/s over representative activity before claiming the original goal complete.

followup_review.user_priority: Prefer existing, newer implementations only where demonstrably efficient; avoid unnecessary protocols/switches/frameworks. Notify user before APK change/restart.
followup_review.large_surface_repair_experiment: Removed from production patch directory; never registered in sources.lock, built as APK or installed. Standalone BufferQueue experiment remains under build/.

standalone_surface_repair.scope: Independent AImageReader/GLES window experiment. Disjoint timer samples excluded. Not active desktop FPS or power evidence.

upstream.decision: Compared actual native diff. Changes concern input/multiwindow/thread naming and a fence timeout; no demonstrated steady-state FPS gain. Do not replace working patched APK merely to update revision.

page_workload.scope: Untraced browser rAF under controlled full-resolution canvas, scrolling, full-text replacement stress; not physical-screen unique-content FPS. Earlier oversized-window test retained separately.

new_backend_trial.decision: Do not change defaults. Initialized hardware backend alone is insufficient; first 600-frame workload did not complete within the CDP deadline. No GPU-crash or software-fallback claim is inferred from timeout.

followup_review.next_action: Use existing frame-sequence, scheduler and submit traces to distinguish main-frame/raster readiness from display-queue pacing at missed updates. No further backend switch or queue enlargement without causal evidence.

pacing_review.deployment: Default APK, library prefix and launcher unchanged; no APK installation or session restart.

trace.interpretation: Swap throttled is a bounded-queue state, not a drop counter or causal proof. The Vulkan output-device source sets max_pending_swaps=1. Existing WSI already uses four images and a two-request display bound; do not blindly add more buffering.
trace.qualification: Instrumented diagnostic data. GPU timestamp window includes barriers and transfer; not isolated copy cost. Browser presentation feedback does not prove physical scanout.

backend_comparison.decision: Keep native default: ANGLE has workload-dependent rAF improvements but 83-92 ms stalls; no overall CPU advantage. No power conclusion. Backend-order trial, not a full thermal/power study.

optimal_layout_candidate.changes: Presentation AHB image LINEAR to OPTIMAL; matching destination-feature check; skip invalid subresource-layout query for optimal image. Existing AHB socket import takes stride from its own descriptor.
optimal_layout_candidate.build: Fresh isolated WSI objects and prefix; unchanged factory Mali and APK.
optimal_layout_candidate.decision: Rejected for production: no page-rate gain (114.41 vs joint baseline 114.96 rAF/s); small transfer-window median difference 1.982 vs 2.064 ms does not establish a useful benefit. Patch unregistered; no default links changed.
optimal_layout_candidate.cleanup: Owned test processes exited; no mappings of the isolated candidate prefix remained. Removed only that experimental prefix; source, objects, patch and evidence retained under build/wsi-optimal-20261017.

uncapped_browser.decision: Rejected: 630-902 rAF/s and roughly 4.6 CPU cores across browser/renderer/GPU, versus roughly 1.5 cores in capped native samples. WSI cap cannot by itself pace browser JavaScript. This is not 120 unique physical frames or a power measurement.
